title: How a Neural Network Learns Part 3

scenes.text: How AI fixes its own mistakes. In part two, we walked downhill to reduce the loss. [1] But with billions of weights, how does each weight know which way to move? [2] In this final part, let's understand backpropagation, without any maths.

Backpropagation is how a network works out who's to blame for a mistake. [1] It sends the error backwards through the network, layer by layer. [2] It starts at the output, where the mistake showed up, [3] works out how much each weight contributed, [4] and tells every weight which way to change.

data.definition: Sending the error backwards through the network to work out how each weight should change.

scenes.text: Here's an analogy. A restaurant gets a bad review, the biryani was too salty. [1] The manager asks the head chef. [2] The head chef traces it back, to the cook who added the salt, and to the recipe card. [3] Then everyone who contributed adjusts a little, the biggest cause the most, and the others less.

Put it all together, and this is how every network trains. [1] The forward pass, where data flows through, and the network makes a guess. [2] The loss, which measures how wrong that guess was. [3] The backward pass, where backpropagation shares out the blame. [4] The update, where every weight takes a small step, with gradient descent. [5] And repeat, millions of times, until the network is good.

data.heading: The training loop
nodes: A small step for every weight

scenes.text: Here are four words to remember. [1] The forward pass, data going in, and a guess coming out. [2] The backward pass, the error going back. [3] The gradient, which direction, and how strongly, each weight should change. [4] And the optimiser, the method that uses gradients to update the weights.

And this explains why training is so expensive. [1] Training needs forward and backward passes, over and over, on huge amounts of data, for weeks. [2] Using a trained model, which is called inference, is just one forward pass per answer.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think AI learns while you chat with it, using backpropagation. [2] Normally, it doesn't. Backpropagation happens during training, done by the company that builds the model. When you chat, the weights stay frozen, and it only does forward passes.

data.myth: AI learns from my chats using backpropagation.
data.fact: Backprop happens during training. When you chat, the weights stay frozen.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Which step sends the error backwards through the network? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] Backpropagation! It shares out the blame, so every weight knows which way to move.

Let's recap. [1] The forward pass makes a guess. [2] The loss measures the mistake. [3] Backpropagation shares out the blame, backwards. [4] And every weight takes a small step to improve. [5] Next, we'll learn the three ways machines learn, supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement. Follow AI Maastaaru!

points: a small step for every weight

post.caption:
Your AI just got it wrong. So which of its billion numbers messed up?

Episode 23 of AI From Scratch: How a Neural Network Learns, Part 3 (backpropagation), explained with a cricket match.
- Last ball, India loses. Who takes the blame?
- Start at the result and walk backwards
- Blame by contribution: batsman 60%, captain 30%, selectors 10%
- Error flows backward, every weight fixes itself a little
- Repeat millions of times and mistakes keep shrinking

Quick test at the end: which layer gets blamed first? Comment your answer.
